descriptionChirho: The proper noun Rephaim (רְפָאִים II), designating an ancient people of great stature who inhabited Canaan and Transjordan before the Israelite conquest. All three clusters represent the same ethnic/tribal referent, differing only in the presence of the definite article and the conjunctive waw: Rephaim, the-Rephaim, and-the-Rephaim. Arabic الرَّفَائِيِّينَ/رَفَائِيمَ (al-Rafā'iyyīn/Rafā'īm), Spanish Refaim/refaítas/refaitas, Hindi रपाईम/रेफ़ैम (Rapā'īm/Refaim), Korean 르바임 (Reuba-im), Swahili Warefaimu/Warefai (with Bantu noun-class prefix Wa- for peoples). Referenced in Genesis 14:5, 15:20, Deuteronomy 2:11-20, 3:11-13, Joshua 12:4, 13:12, 17:15, and 2 Samuel 5:18-22 as pre-Israelite inhabitants associated with the Valley of Rephaim near Jerusalem.
